ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominance of high-intensity pixels (approx. 75-80% white/cream) with high-contrast low-intensity (black) pixels concentrated along the trailing edges and the central peduncle insertion point.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Large contiguous white central zone. High-contrast black pigments are localized as solid banding along the distal trailing edges and a vertical bifurcating stripe extending from the median notch toward the peduncle. Ochre-toned mottling is visible in the mid-lobe regions of both the left and right lobes.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped depression with a calculated pixel angle of approximately 85 degrees; notch vertex is sharp and well-defined.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency micro-serrations along the entire trailing boundary. Significant high-amplitude jagged valleys are visible on the inner right lobe and the outer left lobe, showing irregular pixel-step heights from the surrounding water background.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Lobes exhibit a pronounced convex curve along the leading edges, tapering to sharp distal points (tips), with a moderate concave-to-straight trajectory along the trailing edge leading to the notch.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Two distinct dark, roughly circular pixel clusters located in the upper-distal region of the right lobe. High-intensity white clusters (likely barnacle colonization) are visible at the extreme tip of the left lobe.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Three distinct, sub-parallel dark linear streaks oriented vertically in the lower-central region of the right lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Irregular jaggedness and tissue loss pattern on the right trailing edge, characterized by deeper-than-average U-shaped indentations.
other_distinctive_markers: Extensive diffuse tan/brownish staining (biological film) covering approximately 30% of the visible white ventral surface, most concentrated near the central notch and lobe mid-sections.
